keyFindings.description: Adds a refusal at a process boundary (runtime.kubernetes.pod.env CGO_ENABLED now fails config load) with no `## Contract change census`: searches, every hit with a disposition, and a rollout line naming what an immediate refusal closes.

The ENV's stated reason is false on this image: with gcc present a go/build reader with cgo on succeeds (tester's env -i supervise run, test.json; docs/kubernetes.md:88-91 says so). The `go tool cgo: exit status 2` failure is main's gcc-less image. The LEGION-630 and LEGION-668 learning notes repeat the implication for the eval kernel.

Nothing in the build checks the /opt/go/go.env line that holds acceptance 2 in scrubbed environments (the eval kernel); the PR's own risk line says so. Add `test "$(env -u CGO_ENABLED go env CGO_ENABLED)" = 0` to the toolchain step.
The recipe rebuilds the image ENV by hand with env -i and now lacks CGO_ENABLED=0 (and COREPACK_DEFAULT_TO_LATEST=0), so a go/build reader under it gets cgo on, unlike a pod.
'keeps cgo off by default in every process' overclaims: scrubbed environments do not inherit image ENV.
The 19-line cgo paragraph splits the pinned-downloads bullet from its closing sentence; gcc/libc6-dev belong with the trixie /usr/bin list; '(it only outranks go.env)' has an unclear 'it'.
Supersession is marked with inline bold notes under `status: active`; the repository's convention is frontmatter `status: superseded in part by …`.
